Fixed and verified. Bug: Interval.fromISO called DateTime.fromISO unconditionally, so with Settings.throwOnInvalid = true it threw InvalidDateTimeError before the Duration fallback could run — valid intervals like "2016-01-01/P1Y" and "P1Y/2016-01-01" threw, and bad input leaked the wrong error type. Fix (src/interval.js, fromISO): parse each side in try/catch, track validity, then keep the existing date/duration fallback logic and end at Interval.invalid("unparsable", ...) so invalid input raises InvalidIntervalError. Verified: with throwOnInvalid=true all three ISO forms (date/date, date/duration, duration/date) parse, including with a zone option, and bad inputs throw InvalidIntervalError; with the default setting all bad inputs still return invalid Intervals with invalidReason "unparsable". Full suite: 54/55 suites pass, the only 2 failures are pre-existing ICU French-locale toFormat tests, confirmed failing before the change too.

Fixed and verified. Bug: DateTime#isInDST() compared the current offset against `this.set({ month: 1 }).offset` and `this.set({ month: 5 }).offset` — i.e. the same day-of-month in January/May. In 1974 the USA ran year-round DST (Jan 6 – Oct 27), so for any 1974 date with day-of-month >= 6 both reference dates were themselves in DST, and isInDST() returned false for the whole DST period. Fix (src/datetime.js): pin the January reference to the 1st — `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 }).offset` — which is a standard-time anchor. Verified: every hour of 1974 in America/New_York now matches DST exactly from 1974-01-06T02:00 to 1974-10-27T02:00 (before: only ~54 days correct); normal years (2016–2018 NY: 238 DST days each) and southern-hemisphere zones (Australia/Sydney) are unchanged. Full suite: 54/55 suites, 892/894 tests pass — the only 2 failures are the pre-existing ICU French-locale toFormat tests, identical before and after.
